# shapleydecomp

A model-agnostic decomposition framework for discrete-time simulations.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("aucarter/shapleydecomp")
```

New to the package? Start with the [Get
started](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/articles/shapleydecomp.html)
article. The
[Methods](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/articles/methods.html)
article covers the maths.

## Overview

`shapleydecomp` attributes changes in simulation outcomes to individual
input factors using **Shapley value decomposition**. Any calibrated
discrete-time simulation model can use this package by implementing a
small set of S3 methods.

## Two Counterfactual Types

The package supports two modes of counterfactual analysis:

| Type | `cf_type` | Counterfactual value | Interpretation |
|----|----|----|----|
| **Change since** | `"change_since"` | Value at a baseline year | Impact of *changes in the factor since* the baseline year |
| **Total impact** | `"total_impact"` | Zero / no intervention | *Total* impact of the factor (as if it never existed) |

## Implementing the Interface

To use `shapleydecomp` with your model, create an S3 class and implement
these **required** methods:

``` r

# 1. Run your simulation with given parameters
run_simulation.my_model <- function(model, params, ...) { ... }

# 2. Summarize simulation output into a data.table with a 'year' column
#    plus one column per summary variable (e.g., deaths, infections)
summarize_results.my_model <- function(model, sim_output, ...) { ... }

# 3. Construct counterfactual parameters for a single factor
build_counterfactual.my_model <- function(model, params, factor_name,
                                          decomp_year, cf_type,
                                          baseline_values, ...) { ... }

# 4. Get the baseline value for a factor
get_baseline_value.my_model <- function(model, params, factor_name, cf_type,
                                        baseline_year, ...) { ... }
```

Methods defined at the top level of a script are found by ordinary S3
dispatch. Methods defined anywhere else need registering with
[`.S3method()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/S3method.html). In a package, put
`@export` on each method so that `NAMESPACE` declares it with
`S3method()`.

And these **optional** methods (for performance/setup):

``` r

# One-time preparation before decomp loop (e.g., initial simulation,
# count-to-percentage conversion)
prepare_decomp.my_model <- function(model, params, ...) { ... }

# Warm-start support (avoid re-simulating years before decomp year)
supports_warm_start.my_model <- function(model, ...) { TRUE }
get_warm_start_state.my_model <- function(model, sim_output, year, ...) { ... }
run_from_warm_start.my_model <- function(model, warm_state, params,
                                          output_years, ...) { ... }
```

## Quick Start

``` r

library(shapleydecomp)

# Create your model object (S3 class with methods above)
model <- create_my_model(...)

# Run decomposition
results <- shapley_decompose(
  model        = model,
  params       = my_params,
  factors      = c("treatment_a", "treatment_b", "demographic_x"),
  summary_vars = c("deaths", "infections"),
  decomp_years = 2000:2023,
  method       = "shapley",     # only supported method
  cf_type      = "change_since" # or "total_impact"
)

# Results
results$decomp           # Standard decomposition (factor effects per year)
results$step_scenarios   # All-on time series per decomp year
results$extended_decomp  # Extended decomposition (effects at future years)
results$run_table        # Factorial design table
```

## Validation

Before running a full decomposition, validate that your model correctly
implements the interface:

``` r

validate_model_interface(
  model        = my_model,
  params       = my_params,
  factors      = c("factor_a", "factor_b"),
  summary_vars = c("outcome_1"),
  baseline_year = 2000
)
```

## Decomposition Method

**Shapley value** decomposition weights each factor’s marginal effect by
`1 / (n × C(n-1, k))`, where `k` is the number of other factors in the
“on” state, averaging the factor’s contribution over all coalition sizes
(equivalently, over all factor orderings). This guarantees factor
effects sum to the total difference between the fully-observed and
fully-counterfactual scenarios.

Das Gupta’s symmetric standardization is the special case of the Shapley
value for binary on/off factors and produces identical weights, so
`method = "das_gupta"` is accepted as a deprecated alias for the same
Shapley computation.

# Package index

## Run a decomposition

The entry point and its companions.

- [`shapley_decompose()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/shapley_decompose.md)
  : Run a full decomposition analysis
- [`sequential_totals()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/sequential_totals.md)
  : Total impact per factor at every year from a sequential
  decomposition
- [`validate_model_interface()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/validate_model_interface.md)
  : Validate that a model implements the shapleydecomp interface
- [`CF_CHANGE_SINCE`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/cf_types.md)
  [`CF_TOTAL_IMPACT`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/cf_types.md)
  : Counterfactual type constants

## The model interface

S3 generics your model implements. The first four are required; the rest
are optional and speed things up.

- [`run_simulation()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/run_simulation.md)
  : Run a simulation with the given parameters
- [`summarize_results()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/summarize_results.md)
  : Summarize simulation output into a data.table
- [`get_baseline_value()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/get_baseline_value.md)
  : Get the baseline value for a factor
- [`build_counterfactual()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/build_counterfactual.md)
  : Construct counterfactual parameters for a factor
- [`prepare_decomp()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/prepare_decomp.md)
  : Prepare the model for decomposition
- [`supports_warm_start()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/warm_start.md)
  [`get_warm_start_state()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/warm_start.md)
  [`run_from_warm_start()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/warm_start.md)
  : Warm starts

## Decomposition algebra

Model-free building blocks. Use them directly if you already have
outcomes for every on/off combination.

- [`make_run_table()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/make_run_table.md)
  : Generate the factorial run table for decomposition
- [`run_decomp()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/run_decomp.md)
  : Run decomposition across groups and decomp years
- [`decomp_algebra()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/decomp_algebra.md)
  : Decompose all summary variables for a single group
- [`decomp_pair()`](https://aucarter.github.io/shapleydecomp/reference/decomp_pair.md)
  : Decompose a single summary variable using Shapley value weights
